'''Tournament Guidelines''' is the procedure document for running a Star Wars CCG event.

* Decipher issued a tournament guide (PDF / HTML / text). The 15 April 1997 printing is linked from the 1998 [https://web.archive.org/web/19981205173603/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/tournaments/overview/index.html overview] page. A later shared CCG guide sat on tournaments.decipher.com as tournamentguide-stswyj.
* The Players Committee document in force is [https://res.starwarsccg.org/wp/wp-content/uploads/Star-Wars-CCG-Tournament-Guide-2.2.pdf Official Tournament Guide 2.2] (revised July 2018).


== Players Committee changes ==

* '''2003.''' The Players Committee's four-level Championship Circuit: Level 1 State, National and Provincial Championships (six to eight games of Swiss and a top-2 final; the winner qualified for Day 2 of Worlds), Level 2 Open Qualifiers (eight games and a top-4 playoff; top 2 to Day 2), Level 3 DPC Championship Series events with DeckTech (top 2 to Day 2), and Level 4 the World Championship.<ref name="pc-road03">[https://web.archive.org/web/20030424052746/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/News/Events/roadtoworlds03.htm Road to Worlds Begins in 2003], swccgpc.com. Internet Archive capture 24 April 2003.</ref> Level 1 events cost the director $25 plus shipping of the prize support, with a suggested $5 entry fee, and ran April–June. Level 2 events cost the director $50 plus shipping, with a suggested $10 entry fee, and ran March–September: five to eight in North America and three internationally. Level 3 events had a required $20 entry fee, split by percentage among the top 4, and were planned for Origins, Gen Con, Essen, the European Championships and other events, at least six in all (three in North America, three internationally). Special Events (Grand Slams for SWCCG, [[Young Jedi]] and the [[Jedi Knights Trading Card Game]], [[Classic]] format events and others) were to run February–October, with prizes such as uncut sheets, trophies and Virtual Card sets.<ref name="pc-road03" /> Team tournaments at Origins, Gen Con and Dragon*Con in 2003 were to qualify players for a planned 2004 Regional Team Championship at Gen Con (teams of three from the same region).<ref name="pc-team03">[https://web.archive.org/web/20030809101318/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/News/Events/teamchampionship06122003.htm Team Championship Qualifiers Planned for 2003], swccgpc.com. Internet Archive capture 9 August 2003.</ref> From 1 January 2003 Decipher ratings used a "K" value of 16 for local events, 32 for Level 1, 48 for Level 2 and 64 for Levels 3–4.<ref name="pc-champ0206">[https://web.archive.org/web/20030424053234/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/News/championshipnews02062003.htm 2003 Championship Circuit Opens in One Month], Andrew Howard, swccgpc.com. Internet Archive capture 24 April 2003.</ref> On 18 April 2003, after its ruling on the [[2003 Quebec Provincial Championship]], the Championship Circuit Committee said that updated and revised versions of the Tournament Guidelines and the Code of Conduct were being prepared, and that it hoped to release them before the summer convention season.<ref name="pc-quebec03">[http://www.swccgpc.com/News/quebecruling04182003.htm Championship Circuit Committee's Official Ruling on Quebec Provincial], swccgpc.com (18 April 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20030612201254/http://swccgpc.com:80/News/quebecruling04182003.htm Internet Archive]</ref>
* '''2004.''' The 2004 Championship Series (announced 18 February 2004) had Level 1 States, Provincials and Mini-Opens (winner's bye), Level 2 DPCs, Level 3 Nationals, Continentals, Invitationals and Majors (winner and runner-up byes), and Level 4 Worlds.<ref name="pc-int0404">[https://web.archive.org/web/20040415220046/http://swccgpc.com:80/interior.htm SWCCGPC.com news (December 2003 – April 2004)], swccgpc.com. Internet Archive capture 15 April 2004.</ref>
* '''2005.''' For Worlds 2005 qualifiers, "Tournament directors CANNOT play in their own qualifier, no matter the number of players or if it will avert a bye."<ref name="pc-worlds05">[https://web.archive.org/web/20041216041033/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/News/2005worlds.htm The Road to Worlds 2005], swccgpc.com. Internet Archive capture 16 December 2004.</ref> The same Road to Worlds 2005 announcement said the Advocates were putting together a brand new Star Wars Tournament Guide.<ref name="pc-worlds05" />
* '''1 April 2008.''' Changes announced by [[Michael Erisman]] for the Tournament Committee: a tournament director may play in his own event if he names an assistant judge and a back-up judge (a three-judge system), the event is not a constructed Championship-level event with a cash prize or several Day 2 byes, and he wins no prize other than tournament glass and Day 2 byes; and every Championship-level event must have at least six games.<ref name="pc-sid80">[https://web.archive.org/web/20080712072001/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/modules.php?name=News&file=article&sid=80 Changes to the Tournament Guide - Effect 4/1/08] (28 March 2008), swccgpc.com. Internet Archive capture 12 July 2008.</ref> A playing tournament director must say so in all tournament announcements, naming the two other judges before the first-round pairings, and takes the first-round bye when there is an odd number of players. Events below Championship level need at least four games for Constructed and Squirrel-style events with fewer than eight players and six games with eight or more; Sealed, Cube and Classic (Light Side against Dark Side) events play every opponent with ten or fewer players and six games with more. A tournament director may post an event for the minimum number of games or for six or more, but an event posted for six games must play six.<ref name="pc-sid80" />

History, rating system, command cards, and decklist sheets: [[Tournaments]]. Format names: [[Formats]]. Worlds: [[Championships]].
